primitives.name: Entity Alignment Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions NLev = Lev(entity,title)/max(len(entity),len(title)); z_k = LN(z_token + z_pos + z_seg + z_know).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'NLev': 'dimensionless normalized Levenshtein distance', 'Lev(entity, title)': 'Levenshtein edit distance between entity and title', 'len(entity)': 'character count of entity mention', 'len(title)': 'character count of title'}
primitives.assumptions: String similarity suffices for linking entities; entity mentions are present in candidate set; normalization ensures comparable scales.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When entity or title length approaches zero, NLev becomes undefined.

layer2.mapping: Maps textual alignment to semantic coherence in summarization; GSI uses this to assess knowledge relevance during belief updating.

primitives.name: Knowledge Fusion Embedding
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions NLev = Lev(entity,title)/max(len(entity),len(title)); z_k = LN(z_token + z_pos + z_seg + z_know).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'z_k': 'contextualized embedding vector', 'z_token': 'token-level embedding', 'z_pos': 'positional embedding', 'z_seg': 'segment embedding', 'z_know': 'knowledge-aware embedding'}
primitives.assumptions: Embeddings are additive; knowledge embeddings preserve semantic meaning; layer normalization stabilizes training.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If any component is missing, fusion quality degrades significantly.

layer2.mapping: Generates enriched sentence representations for summarization; GSE leverages this kernel to compute narrative transitions.

The core innovation lies in integrating structured knowledge into summarization through a dual-stage process: first, aligning entities using string similarity and computing NLev to ensure semantic fidelity; second, fusing knowledge embeddings into a contextualized representation z_k. This enables the model to generate richer summaries by retrieving relevant facts from a curated knowledge base. The ablation studies confirm that removing knowledge components significantly degrades performance, indicating robustness of the approach. However, the system suffers from hallucination due to incorrect knowledge injection, suggesting a need for fact-checking mechanisms. The failure mode occurs when knowledge is misaligned or outdated, leading to false positives in generated content.
